content.text:
Yes, mathematically options **a** and **b** define the same signal here.

At the shared boundary,

- left rule: $2t$ gives $2(1)=2$
- right rule: $3-t$ gives $3-1=2$

So whether $t=1$ belongs to the left piece or the right piece, $x(1)=2$ either way.

The reason the quiz marks **a** is that the prompt explicitly says:

> Use the left segment for $-1\le t<1$ and the right segment for $1\le t\le3$.

So **a** matches that requested interval assignment exactly. But if the question were simply “Which definition matches the graph?”, then **b** is also valid because the formulas agree at the joining point.

Endpoint placement only matters when the two formulas give different values at that boundary, or when the graph shows an open/closed endpoint distinction.
